t: ff.58 Do bananas pollute too much?
st: How to cut and track the emissions of everyday activities

sec.t: ff.58.1 The cost of a human life
sec.p: In How Bad Are Bananas?, Mike Berners-Lee, professor at Lancaster University, breaks down the ecological cost of practically everything. With chapters sorting objects and activities by g/kg/t of CO2 emitted, the author calculates the impact of: a mortgage, a road accident, the…
If you want a visual idea of what 10 tonnes look like, gaze at the Po Valley from the Orobic Prealps (but if you can't, there's a game, Seeing CO2).

sec.t: ff.58.3 Going to Niagara Falls (from New York)
sec.p: To show the level of detail the author reaches in calculating emissions, which are very often indirect and “invisible”, here's an example.

Money emissions. On average, spending a dollar contributes 100g-1kg (or at most 10kg). So a starting point for polluting less is probably frugality. Or a life of excess at 30 t, offset with 140 euros in reforestation projects and by investing in renewables (!!!).

sec.t: ff.58.5 Happy degrowth or tech growth?
sec.p: On the one hand, less excess and waste is desirable, but it's neither the only nor the main solution for a fortissimo future.
